name: GET /api/leadflow/events/status - how far the consumer has got
description:
Advances the pipeline projection and reports where it now stands: how many events were applied, how many were dead-lettered, the checkpoint sequence, and a stable fingerprint of the whole projection.

THE FINGERPRINT IS THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION MADE OBSERVABLE (AC1). 'Killing the consumer mid-stream and restarting produces byte-identical projection state' is only checkable if the state has a stable identity, so it is an md5 over the projection's columns ordered by subject - not a row-to-JSON, which would depend on physical row order and on how the driver serialises a timestamp.

ADVANCING ON A READ is deliberate. The consumer is a catch-up mechanism rather than the primary path - the receiver folds inline and a background tick covers the rest - so making the status call advance means an operator asking 'where are we?' cannot be told a number that is stale because nothing has polled recently. It is idempotent: a second call applies nothing.

Behind authenticate rather than governed: the payload is sequences and counts, with no subject to make a governed decision about. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: Reports the checkpoint and a projection fingerprint
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer. Verified against the running server rather than assumed.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify. Distinct from UNAUTHENTICATED because the caller's fix differs: attach a token versus refresh one.
